findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes when paginating AuditLogEntry.datetime
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get passes paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField (datetime.datetime). Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor(value) / math.ceil(value) directly on the datetime attribute, which raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime. In addition, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it to a timezone-aware datetime object, causing subsequent SQL comparisons against the timestamp column to fail.

findings.title: Unconditional access to organization_context.member raises AttributeError when member is None
findings.body: enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated on every GET request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint. When request.user.is_superuser is False and organization_context.member is None (for example, with organization-scoped API tokens or non-member contexts), accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'. Furthermore, checking request.user.is_superuser directly instead of is_active_superuser(request) bypasses active superuser session validation, and member.has_global_access is True for all members when an organization has open membership enabled, not just administrators.

findings.title: Slicing a Django QuerySet with a negative start_offset raises ValueError
findings.body: Both BasePaginator.get_result (lines 182-184, when cursor.is_prev is True and cursor.offset < 0) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (lines 877-886, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0) pass a negative start_offset into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexing and immediately raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."), resulting in an unhandled 500 error whenever a cursor with a negative offset is supplied. Additionally, when cursor.is_prev is False and offset < 0, clamping start_offset = max(0, offset) while keeping offset negative corrupts downstream slice-trimming (len(results) == offset + limit + extra) and next-cursor offset calculations in build_cursor.

findings.title: Evicting spans via zpopmin leaks redirect entries in span-buf:sr and ignores max_segment_spans
findings.body: In add-buffer.lua, every incoming span_id is inserted into the redirect hash main_redirect_key (span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}) on line 40, and then lines 62-64 evict spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise via zpopmin when span_count exceeds 1000. Because SpansBuffer.done_flush_segments only calls HDEL on span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id} for spans present in the flushed segment, the redirect hash entries for all evicted spans are never deleted upon flush and remain in Redis until the 1-hour TTL expires. Additionally, if the root/segment span has an earlier end_timestamp_precise than async child spans, zpopmin will evict the root span itself while leaving span-buf:hrs set to 1. Finally, the limit of 1000 is hardcoded in Lua rather than using SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans, leaving the max_segment_spans attribute on SpansBuffer dead.

findings.title: No test coverage for span eviction when a segment exceeds 1000 spans
findings.body: The PR replaces the read-time max_segment_spans check in SpansBuffer._load_segment_data with write-time eviction via zpopmin in add-buffer.lua when a segment exceeds 1000 spans, but tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py only updates existing 4-5 span test fixtures with end_timestamp_precise and adds no test verifying eviction behavior above 1000 spans.
